extracted.intended_audience: writers of all skill levels using Scribophile (authors, beta readers, critique partners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to use Scribophile’s features to build a writing habit, learn craft, get and give peer critiques, manage beta reads, and find critique partners. Covers which site areas to use (Writing Together, Writing Academy, Main/Personal/Beta Read Spotlights, Groups, Beta Reader Directory) and some procedural tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a daily writing habit (Writing Together)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in our free daily online writing sprint, Writing Together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The best way to start learning to write is by keeping a daily writing habit. You don’t have to know a thing about writing to show up and put a few words down on the page — it’s the habit that’s important. Writing Together is perfect for building and maintaining a writing habit and for keeping up momentum while drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study craft in the Writing Academy
rubrics_metrics.description: Read about the craft in our free Writing Academy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To start learning the fundamentals, check out our free Writing Academy for hundreds of articles covering everything from the basics to advanced topics. The Academy covers principles of storytelling (character archetypes, plot arcs, dialogue, and everything in-between) to help perfect your craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Writing Forums to connect and learn
rubrics_metrics.description: Chat with writers in our Writing Forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Forums are where writers of all skill levels meet to chat; they’re busy 24×7. Fill out your personal profile, see what people are discussing, ask your own questions, and make friends. Use forums to discuss the writing life and your progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill out your personal profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out your personal profile to engage with the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A completed profile helps you see discussions, ask questions, and make friends — making it easier to dive into groups, forums, and other community activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice with the weekly Writing Challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice with our free weekly Writing Challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Monday Scribophile posts a new writing prompt to inspire a short story. These challenges aren’t graded or critiqued — they’re a judgement-free way to practice your writing muscle and to see how other members approached the same prompt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give feedback to learn (critique as training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving feedback is one of the best ways of learning how to look at your own writing with a critical eye.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don’t have to be a pro to tell a writer what did or didn’t work — anyone can give feedback, even if they’ve never done it before. Giving critiques also earns karma points. Check out the site’s guide to writing a great critique for pointers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the guide to writing a great critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the site’s 'guide to writing a great critique' when giving feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide contains lots of helpful pointers on how to structure critiques and what to focus on when commenting on other members’ work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit any writing for feedback (general acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit some writing for feedback — poems, flash fiction, short stories, nonfiction, drafts of any stage are accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The heart of Scribophile is the feedback system, which gets you guaranteed feedback on your writing from writers all over the world. You can submit anything at all for feedback — it doesn’t have to be a totally finished work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Main Spotlight for guaranteed critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit chapters for feedback to the Main Spotlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main Spotlight is where you can post your work for guaranteed feedback without having to meet or manage readers. You can post anything, from early drafts to polished revisions. Read about how to post your first work for critique and about how the karma point system works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Personal Spotlight for trusted critique partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Get feedback from a group of trusted critique partners in your Personal Spotlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once you’ve joined some groups and made friends, post your work to the Personal Spotlight to get more critiques for your karma point spend. The Personal Spotlight awards maximum karma points to your followers and groupmates, and you get 6 critiques instead of 3 for the Main Spotlight — but the tradeoff is that your posts aren’t visible in site listings, so you have to personally ask your friends and groupmates to critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Join groups to find genre-specific peers
rubrics_metrics.description: Join groups to share your writing with writers with the same interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups are a great way to meet and chat with other writers who are reading and writing the same kind of stories that you are. Each group has its own discussion forum and you can join as many groups as you like to meet potential critique partners and beta readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post full novels in Beta Read Spotlight for full-novel exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Post your novel for free in the Beta Read Spotlight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Beta Read Spotlight is designed to facilitate full-novel exchanges with trusted beta readers. You can post your entire novel without having to earn or spend karma points. Beta readers can give chapter-by-chapter feedback using the critiquing system, and you can keep track of feedback with your novel’s Critique Overview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Beta Reader Directory to recruit beta readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse the Beta Reader Directory to directly query beta readers interested in your genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The directory lists tens of thousands of readers; you can search by interest, genre, and specialty. Once a beta reader accepts your query, you can send them a link to your manuscript posted in the Beta Read Spotlight and manage your beta readers directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill out a Beta Reader Profile to be recruited
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out your Beta Reader Profile so authors can contact you to beta read their books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors browse the Beta Reader Directory and will contact you based on your genre interests and specialties to request free beta reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browse Main Spotlight to find work to critique immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse the Main Spotlight for work that you can read and critique immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main Spotlight is the centerpiece where authors post their writing to get feedback; readers and critics can choose pieces to critique right away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Critique Overview to track feedback on novels
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep track of feedback all in one place with your novel’s Critique Overview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Beta Read Spotlight and chapter-by-chapter feedback, Critique Overview helps you organize and review comments and suggestions across the whole manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Karma points as the site’s exchange mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Karma points are earned by giving feedback and are used to request critiques; different spotlights interact with karma differently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Giving feedback earns karma points. Main Spotlight posts generate 3 critiques; Personal Spotlight costs karma but yields 6 critiques and awards maximum karma points to followers/groupmates. Beta Read Spotlight allows posting entire novels without earning/spending karma points. Read 'how our karma point system works' for details.
